gate_semantics: Existence of at least one scientific foundation model relevant to the candidate environment; benchmark-specific demonstrated benefit is not required.
primary_evidence: The official paper title is 'Intern-S1: A Scientific Multimodal Foundation Model'.
Intern-S1 combines a Qwen3 MoE language model and InternViT vision encoder and is further pretrained on multimodal data including scientific-domain tokens.
The official paper reports MatBench 75.0 and materials-science-relevant professional tasks, including thermodynamic stability prediction for crystals.

MATRIX.paper_evidence: The official MATRIX paper introduces the materials-science benchmark and corresponding MATRIX-PT text, vision, and full post-trained Qwen models; it reports 10-25% experimental-interpretation and 5-16% text-reasoning gains from visual supervision.

BioReason-Pro_GO.primary_evidence: The official release describes a multimodal reasoning LLM for protein function prediction, integrating ESM3 protein embeddings, a GO graph encoder, InterPro/STRING biological context, and Qwen3-4B; public SFT and RL checkpoints are released.
BioReason-Pro_GO.task_scope_caveat: The qualification task is the distinct nonvisual Gene Ontology annotation-recovery endpoint, not an evaluation of BioReason-Pro free-form summaries or structure-image reasoning.

caveat: Intern-S1 establishes a named multimodal scientific foundation model with materials relevance only. It does not establish fit, improvement, or successful tool integration on MATCHA, CSMBench, or OmniMatBench specifically. MATRIX and BioReason-Pro instead have directly associated released domain models documented above.
